sentences.en: Across the country, millions of Americans with unpaid student loans are discovering that years of patience and forgiveness from the U.S.
sentences.zh: 在全国范围内，数百万背负未偿学生贷款的美国人发现，美国政府多年来的耐心与宽容

sentences.en: government have officially come to an end.
sentences.zh: 已经正式画上了句号。

sentences.en: Today, Stacey Cowley on what's behind the change of heart, its financial consequences for borrowers, and the larger reckoning that it could finally trigger
sentences.zh: 今天，斯黛西·考利将带我们探讨这一态度转变背后的原因、对借款人的财务后果，以及它最终可能引发的更广泛的清算

sentences.en: about how Americans pay for higher education.
sentences.zh: 关于美国人如何支付高等教育费用。

sentences.en: It's Monday, April 21St.
sentences.zh: 今天是4月21日，星期一。

sentences.en: Well, Stacey, it's nice to have you back.
sentences.zh: 斯黛西，很高兴你能回来。

sentences.en: Thanks for having me.
sentences.zh: 谢谢邀请我来。

sentences.en: I think this is the third time that we have had a version of this conversation with you.
sentences.zh: 我想这已经是我们第三次和你进行这种形式的谈话了。

sentences.en: Fourth, I think.
sentences.zh: 第四次，我想。

sentences.en: Oh, excuse me.
sentences.zh: 哦，不好意思。

sentences.en: There's a lot of developments along the way.
sentences.zh: 这期间发生了许多变化。

sentences.en: Well, that's right.
sentences.zh: 嗯，确实如此。

sentences.en: I mean, we keep coming to you to talk about this subject because you're the authority on it and because it keeps changing.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我们一直找你谈这个话题，因为你是这方面的权威，而且情况一直在变。

sentences.en: And at this point, it's genuinely confusing.
sentences.zh: 而且在这个节点上，这真的让人感到困惑。

sentences.en: And it's extremely important to tens of millions of people.
sentences.zh: 对数以千万计的人来说，这也极其重要。

sentences.en: So I'm preemptively grateful.
sentences.zh: 所以我提前表示感谢。

sentences.en: Well, thank you for your intereSt.
sentences.zh: 好的，谢谢你的关注。

sentences.en: So where exactly are we right now in this long, winding saga of America's student loans?
sentences.zh: 那么，在这场漫长而曲折的美国学生贷款传奇中，我们现在究竟处于什么位置？

sentences.en: So we're at a real turning point on this.
sentences.zh: 我们在这一点上迎来了真正的转折点。

sentences.en: After this nearly five-year period when most people weren't making payments and weren't required to do so and weren't having any negative consequences,
sentences.zh: 在经历了将近五年的大多数人不用还款、不需要这么做且没有任何负面后果的时期之后，

sentences.en: if they didn't, the government really dropped the hammer in the last few months.
sentences.zh: 如果他们不还，政府在过去几个月里真的动真格了。

sentences.en: They've said, we are done with timeouts.
sentences.zh: 他们说，我们受够了暂停。

sentences.en: We're done with pauses.
sentences.zh: 我们受够了缓冲期。

sentences.en: You need to start paying again.
sentences.zh: 你们必须开始重新还款了。

sentences.en: That's a very big change.
sentences.zh: 这是一个非常大的改变。

sentences.en: And they instructed their loan servicers to start reporting delinquencies to the credit bureaus again, which hasn't happened for five years now.
sentences.zh: 他们指示贷款服务机构开始向征信机构重新报告逾期情况，这已经五年没发生了。

sentences.en: So that immediately resulted in four million people found delinquencies reported on their credit reports.
sentences.zh: 所以这直接导致了四百万人的信用报告中出现了逾期记录。

sentences.en: And these are serious delinquencies.
sentences.zh: 而且这些都是严重的逾期。

sentences.en: People saw their credit scores plunge.
sentences.zh: 人们看到他们的信用评分暴跌。

sentences.en: That can have immediate impacts on your ability to rent an apartment, to get a mortgage, to get a loan for a car.
sentences.zh: 这会直接影响你租公寓、申请抵押贷款以及申请汽车贷款的能力。

sentences.en: So this can be pretty catastrophic when this happens to you.
sentences.zh: 所以这种事发生在你身上时，可能是相当灾难性的。

sentences.en: And we've had four million people who are now in that delinquency.
sentences.zh: 我们现在已经有四百万人陷入了这种逾期状态。

sentences.en: The estimates are that we're going to have as many as nine million by the end of this year, and that many of those people could end up in default.
sentences.zh: 据估计，到今年年底，这一数字将高达九百万，其中许多人可能会最终违约。

sentences.en: That's what happens when you don't pay for at least nine months.
sentences.zh: 这就是至少九个月不还款的后果。

sentences.en: And that sets off a whole other series of very bad financial consequences.
sentences.zh: 而这会引发一连串非常糟糕的财务后果。

sentences.en: And if we do end up with nine million people defaulting, that would be a record number.
sentences.zh: 如果我们最终有九百万人的贷款违约，那将是一个纪录。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And it would also mean we have nine million Americans who are basically in the worst kind of financial bind you can be in.
sentences.zh: 这也意味着我们将有九百万美国人基本上陷入了你能想象到的最糟糕的财务困境中。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And even beyond that, the repayment really hasn't gone as planned.
sentences.zh: 不仅如此，实际的还款情况并没有按计划进行。

sentences.en: Right now, of the roughly 38 million borrowers who have payments due and are supposed to be making payments.
sentences.zh: 目前，在大约3800万名有到期还款且本应还款的借款人中，

sentences.en: Yeah, it's a big number.
sentences.zh: 是的，这是一个庞大的数字。

sentences.en: So of those 38 million, right now only about a third are making payments.
sentences.zh: 所以在这些3800万人中，目前只有大约三分之一的人在还款。

sentences.en: I think it's important to have you remind us briefly how we got here, because a lot of factors went into how we arrived in this moment.
sentences.zh: 我觉得有必要请你简要回顾一下我们是如何走到这一步的，因为很多因素导致了我们走到今天这个时刻。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So this federal student loan payment system has always been kind of rocky.
sentences.zh: 这个联邦学生贷款还款系统一直有点坎坷。

sentences.en: It has never really worked particularly smoothly for the last decade and a half.
sentences.zh: 在过去十五年里，它从来没有真正顺利运转过。

sentences.en: But what happened when the pandemic started back in March 2020 was the government immediately called an emergency timeout.
sentences.zh: 但在2020年3月大流行开始时，政府立即宣布了紧急暂停。

sentences.en: In response to kind of the economic conditions at the time, they said, all right, we're going to take this burden away from people.
sentences.zh: 为了应对当时的经济状况，他们说，好吧，我们要为人们卸下这个沉重的负担。

sentences.en: You don't have to make these payments.
sentences.zh: 你们不必偿还这些贷款。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Huge deal.
sentences.zh: 一件大事。

sentences.en: And kind of understandable because it was the federal government that shut our economy down.
sentences.zh: 而且这也情有可原，因为是联邦政府关闭了我们的经济。

sentences.en: And so the thinking was, we're going to not force a lot of people who are out of work or making a lot less than usual to have this burden on top of that.
sentences.zh: 所以当时的考量是，我们不应该强迫许多失业或收入大不如前的人在背负这些的基础上，还要承担这份负担。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.en: There were record unemployment numbers.
sentences.zh: 当时失业率创下了纪录。

sentences.en: And one thing about this is not only was the government the one that shut things down, they are also the creditor for all of these student loans.
sentences.zh: 关于这一点，不仅政府是关闭经济的幕后推手，它也是所有这些学生贷款的债权人。

sentences.en: It's a very unusual market in that they don't have to go to banks.
sentences.zh: 这是一个非常不寻常的市场，借款人不必去找银行。

sentences.en: They don't have to go to private lenders.
sentences.zh: 他们不必去找私人贷款机构。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: They were providing the loans.
sentences.zh: 是政府在提供贷款。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 正是如此。

sentences.en: It wasn't a temporary measure, but it kept getting extended.
sentences.zh: 这不是一项临时措施，但它一直被延长。

sentences.en: First by President Trump.
sentences.zh: 首先是由特朗普总统延长的。

sentences.en: Mm-hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯哼。

sentences.en: So Trump extended it several times.
sentences.zh: 所以特朗普多次延长了它。

sentences.en: Then President Biden took office, and he extended it several times.
sentences.zh: 然后拜登总统上台，他又多次延长了它。

sentences.en: And it just kept going and going and going.
sentences.zh: 它就这样一次又一次地持续下去。

sentences.en: And so for how long were, I think, tens of millions, right, of folks who had lots of student loan debt permitted to not make repayments?
sentences.zh: 那么，我想有数千万，对吧，背负大量学生贷款债务的人被允许不用偿还贷款，持续了多久？

sentences.en: So it officially stretched for about four years until September 2023.
sentences.zh: 它官方持续了大约四年，直到2023年9月。

sentences.en: But then President Biden added an additional thing to this.
sentences.zh: 但随后拜登总统又增加了一项规定。

sentences.en: He said, for the next year, all right, you're supposed to be making payments.
sentences.zh: 他说，在接下来的一年里，好吧，你们本该开始还款了。

sentences.en: We're going to try to collect, but we're not going to report you to the credit bureaus if you don't.
sentences.zh: 我们会尝试催收，但如果你们不还，我们不会向征信机构报告你们的逾期。

sentences.en: I'm going to guess a lot of people took advantage of that.
sentences.zh: 我猜很多人都利用了这一点。

sentences.en: There wasn't a lot of negative consequences if you just didn't start paying.
sentences.zh: 如果你只是不开始还款，并不会产生太多的负面后果。

sentences.en: So a lot of people didn't.
sentences.zh: 所以很多人都没有还。

sentences.en: And adding to that was the confusion around what was going to happen to this debt.
sentences.zh: 除此之外，还有关于这笔债务将如何处理的混乱局面。

sentences.en: I mean, President Biden was pursuing the plan of mass debt cancellation up to $20,000 per borrower.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，拜登总统一直在推行大规模债务减免计划，每位借款人最高可减免2万美元。

sentences.en: The Supreme Court then overturned that.
sentences.zh: 随后最高法院推翻了该计划。

sentences.en: And all of these people who thought their debts might go away entirely got that disappointment.
sentences.zh: 所有这些以为自己的债务可能会彻底一笔勾销的人都感到了失望。

sentences.en: And then President Biden moved on to his plan B, which was introducing a new repayment plan called SAVE that was much more generous than any past payment plan.
sentences.zh: 接着拜登总统推出了他的B计划，即引入一项名为SAVE的新还款计划，该计划比以往任何还款计划都要宽厚得多。

sentences.en: How much more generous?
sentences.zh: 宽厚多少？

sentences.en: Well, it was an income-driven payment plan, meaning that your payments would be directly tied to how much you were making.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这是一个收入驱动的还款计划，意味着你的还款额将与你的收入直接挂钩。

sentences.en: It was deliberately an attempt to keep things affordable.
sentences.zh: 这完全是为了让人们能够负担得起而做出的尝试。

sentences.en: And on past payment plans, that's typically been limited to about 10 percent of your discretionary income.
sentences.zh: 在过去的还款计划中，这一比例通常被限制在可支配收入的10%左右。

sentences.en: President Biden's plan cut that in half for people with only undergraduate loans.
sentences.zh: 拜登总统的计划为仅有本科贷款的人将这一比例砍半。

sentences.en: So suddenly people whose payments were 10 percent of, you know, their income were cut down to 5 percent.
sentences.zh: 所以突然之间，那些还款额占收入10%的人，其比例降到了5%。

sentences.en: That's a huge change.
sentences.zh: 这是一个巨大的改变。

sentences.en: There's just a lot of amnesty kind of built into the messaging in the system.
sentences.zh: 这种传达的信息和系统中内嵌了大量的宽大处理。

sentences.en: But, of course, Trump and his allies on the campaign trail, and I watched this closely, were making the argument, wait a minute,
sentences.zh: 但是，当然，特朗普和他在竞选活动中的盟友们——我一直在密切关注这一点——都在争辩，等一下，

sentences.en: why is student debt being treated with all this forgiveness?
sentences.zh: 凭什么学生债务能得到这么多的豁免？

sentences.en: Nothing like that happens to auto debt or mortgage debt.
sentences.zh: 汽车贷款或抵押贷款可没有这种待遇。

sentences.en: So why college debt?
sentences.zh: 那为什么偏偏是大学债务？

sentences.en: And to Trump, out of office at this point, it felt like a Democratic president handing out gifts to Democratic kind of people.
sentences.zh: 对当时已经不在台上的特朗普来说，这感觉就像是一个民主党总统在向民主党阵营的人派发福利。

sentences.en: Mm-hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯哼。

sentences.en: There's a real political divide around here.
sentences.zh: 这周围存在着真正的政治分歧。

sentences.en: And the reality of the demographics don't always bear it out.
sentences.zh: 而人口统计的现实并不总能支持这种说法。

sentences.en: A lot of the people who do have debt, it is a lot of people who are working class.
sentences.zh: 很多背负债务的人，其实都是工薪阶层。

sentences.en: And a lot of people have amounts from things like trade schools and professional schools that they haven't been able to pay off.
sentences.zh: 许多人还背负着来自贸易学校和专业学校等无法偿还的债务金额。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So plenty of people in the Trump coalition have student debt.
sentences.zh: 所以特朗普阵营里也有很多人背负着学生贷款。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: But it was definitely clear that Trump had a very different vision for this than President Biden did, and that if he were to come back to office,
sentences.zh: 但显然，特朗普对此有着与拜登总统截然不同的构想，如果他重返白宫，

sentences.en: that a lot of what Biden had built was going to go away.
sentences.zh: 拜登建立的许多成果都将不复存在。

sentences.en: OK.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: So let's fast forward to the part where Trump does come back to office.
sentences.zh: 那么让我们快进到特朗普重返白宫的部分。

sentences.en: What exactly does he do?
sentences.zh: 他到底做了什么？

sentences.en: What does he change?
sentences.zh: 他改变了什么？

sentences.en: What does he take away?
sentences.zh: 他取消了什么？

sentences.en: And what remains?
sentences.zh: 又有什么保留了下来？

sentences.en: So even before Trump comes back to power, the plan that Biden introduced, the SAVE plan, got caught up in court.
sentences.zh: 因此，甚至在特朗普重新掌权之前，拜登推出的那个计划，即SAVE计划，就已经陷入了法庭诉讼之中。

sentences.en: A group of Republican-led states challenged it, said to succeed at the president's authority, and that has been prevailing in court,
sentences.zh: 一群由共和党领导的州对其提出了质疑，称其超出了总统的职权范围，并且这一诉求在法庭上占了上风，

sentences.en: which left about 8 million borrowers who had signed up for this plan kind of in limbo, waiting to see what was going to happen with these court cases.
sentences.zh: 这使得大约800万注册了该计划的借款人陷入了进退维谷的境地，等待着这些诉讼的结果。

sentences.en: So once Trump returns to office, it becomes clear that the plan is doomed.
sentences.zh: 所以一旦特朗普重返白宫，这个计划显然就注定要失败了。

sentences.en: SAVE is doomed.
sentences.zh: SAVE计划完蛋了。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 正是如此。

sentences.en: Either the courts are going to kill it or the president and his administration are going to kill it, but it's going to go away.
sentences.zh: 要么是法院废除它，要么是总统及其政府废除它，但它肯定是要消失的。

sentences.en: Which is pretty whipsaw-ish.
sentences.zh: 这真是令人应接不暇。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And those 8 million borrowers are all still just on pause right now.
sentences.zh: 而那800万借款人目前都仍然处于暂停还款状态。

sentences.en: Mm-hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯哼。

sentences.en: But for all these other tens of millions of borrowers, the message is you need to be paying.
sentences.zh: 但对于其他所有数千万的借款人来说，传达的信息是你们必须开始还款了。

sentences.en: Mm-hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯哼。

sentences.en: Biden had set it up so that payments were going to resume right after the election, kind of no matter what happened.
sentences.zh: 拜登此前做出的安排是，无论发生什么，还款都将在大选结束后立即恢复。

sentences.en: That meant that Trump gets elected, he's coming into office, just as this years of not really having to pay ends,
sentences.zh: 这意味着特朗普当选并上台的时机，正值多年无需实质还款的时期结束之际，

sentences.en: and as the government gets serious about collecting on these debts.
sentences.zh: 也正值政府开始认真催收这些债务之时。

sentences.en: However, people have been warning for years that getting people to start paying again after years of not paying was going to be really tricky.
sentences.zh: 然而，多年来人们一直在警告说，在经历了多年的不还款之后，让人们重新开始还款将是非常棘手的。

sentences.en: It was going to require a lot of resources and a lot of attention.
sentences.zh: 这需要耗费大量的资源和精力。

sentences.en: And that is not what is happening.
sentences.zh: 但现实并非如此。

sentences.en: The student loan servicers who are supposed to be collecting these debts are pretty hammered and overwhelmed,
sentences.zh: 本应负责催收这些债务的学生贷款服务机构已经精疲力竭、不堪重负，

sentences.en: and they have been struggling to get guidance from the education department.
sentences.zh: 并且一直在艰难地从教育部那里获取指导意见。

sentences.en: Because Trump is trying to shut it down.
sentences.zh: 因为特朗普正试图叫停它。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.en: And one of the things borrowers are now confronting is not only do you have to start paying this bill again, but you also have to navigate what's the best way to pay it.
sentences.zh: 现在借款人面临的问题之一不仅是你要重新开始支付这笔账单，还得摸索出最佳的还款方式是什么。

sentences.en: And that's been one of the areas where borrowers have been running into challenges.
sentences.zh: 这也是借款人遇到困难的领域之一。

sentences.en: They have been trying to get themselves back into repayments, and there is currently an enormous backlog at the education department.
sentences.zh: 他们一直在努力恢复还款，而教育部目前积压了大量的工作。

sentences.en: A lot of people have already left, either by being fired or retiring or just deciding to opt out.
sentences.zh: 很多人已经离职了，有的是被解雇的，有的是退休了，还有的只是决定退出。

sentences.en: So that agency is currently very hollowed out.
sentences.zh: 所以那个机构现在非常空心化。

sentences.en: One of the offices that has really been decimated over there is an office that handles student loan borrower complaints.
sentences.zh: 那里受打击最严重的办公室之一，是负责处理学生贷款借款人投诉的办公室。

sentences.en: One of the people who was fired last month from that office said in court filings that she left behind a backlog of 16,000 complaints.
sentences.zh: 上个月被该办公室解雇的一名员工在法庭文件中称，她留下了16,000起积压的投诉。

sentences.en: Oh, my gosh.
sentences.zh: 天哪。

sentences.en: That are piled up and unaddressed.
sentences.zh: 堆积如山，无人处理。

sentences.en: The education department also has more than a million borrowers who have applied for income-driven payment and are stuck in limbo.
sentences.zh: 教育部还有超过一百万名申请了收入驱动型还款的借款人，他们的申请陷入了进退维谷的境地。

sentences.en: They're waiting for their applications to be processed.
sentences.zh: 他们正在等待申请得到处理。

sentences.en: There's a huge backlog, often stretching from months.
sentences.zh: 积压情况极其严重，往往持续数月之久。

sentences.en: So those people are also kind of stuck right now.
sentences.zh: 所以这些人现在也处于某种进退两难的境地。

sentences.en: This is where the doge job cut rubber meets the road.
sentences.zh: 这就是政府效率部（DOGE）裁员真正见真章的时候了。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: At exactly the moment when you would ideally want to be staffing up and putting more resources into the system to help people navigate this return to repayment,
sentences.zh: 在理想情况下，你本最希望扩充人员、向系统投入更多资源来帮助人们应对恢复还款的这个时刻，

sentences.en: we've instead done the opposite.
sentences.zh: 我们却反其道而行之。

sentences.en: I'm going to assume that you have spoken to some borrowers who, when they've been told now they have to start repaying, are trying to do that.
sentences.zh: 我猜你一定和一些借款人交谈过，他们在被告知现在必须开始还款时，正试图这样做。

sentences.en: And I wonder what the math looks like in their financial life all of a sudden.
sentences.zh: 我想知道，他们突然间的财务生活里，这些账目究竟是怎么算的。

sentences.en: It's a real struggle for a lot of people.
sentences.zh: 对许多人来说，这真的是一场挣扎。

sentences.en: Thank you so much for taking the time to talk with me about this.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢你抽出时间和我谈论这件事。

sentences.en: Oh, no problem.
sentences.zh: 噢，没问题。

sentences.en: Yeah, it's been quite, um, yeah.
sentences.zh: 对，这真的是……嗯，对。

sentences.en: I spoke to a health care worker down in Florida who's been trying to get enrolled in the income-driven repayment.
sentences.zh: 我采访了佛罗里达州的一名医护人员，她一直在努力注册收入驱动型还款。

sentences.en: I do work two jobs because I'm kind of trying to prepare for that student loan payment.
sentences.zh: 我确实打两份工，因为我有点在为那笔学生贷款的还款做准备。

sentences.en: But again...
sentences.zh: 但话说回来……

sentences.en: She did the math on the government's own calculator and worked out that her payments would be about $490 a month.
sentences.zh: 她用政府自己的计算器算了算账，算出她每个月的还款额大约是490美元。

sentences.en: She said that would be a stretch, but she could make that work.
sentences.zh: 她说这会有些吃力，但她还能应付。

sentences.en: Then I get a bill in January that was for like $924.
sentences.zh: 然后我在一月份收到了一张账单，大概是924美元。

sentences.en: However, when she got her first bill, she found that something had gone awry and she was getting a bill for the standard payment amount.
sentences.zh: 然而，当她收到第一张账单时，她发现出了问题，她收到的账单金额是标准还款额。

sentences.en: And I'm like, this isn't right because this is not what it should be.
sentences.zh: 当时我就想，这不对劲，因为这不应该是这个数字。

sentences.en: Like, it should be much lower.
sentences.zh: 比如说，它应该低得多。

sentences.en: Which is not a bill she can deal with.
sentences.zh: 这不是她能应付的账单。

sentences.en: I mean, I'm making decent income, but still, it's never enough to keep up with that.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我的收入还算 decent（体面/不错），但即便如此，也永远赶不上这笔开销。

sentences.en: So she's been calling her servicer and spending hours and hours on hold, multiple days for the last few weeks trying to get this fixed.
sentences.zh: 因此，在过去的几周里，她一直在给贷款服务机构打电话，一等就是好几个小时，一连好几天，试图解决这个问题。

sentences.en: You know, their systems are all messed up.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，他们的系统全乱套了。

sentences.en: To know what's actually going on behind the scenes, it's almost like you're guessing what...
sentences.zh: 要想知道幕后到底发生了什么，简直就像是在盲目猜测……

sentences.en: And it just keeps going awry at every turn.
sentences.zh: 而且每一步都在出岔子。

sentences.en: She got a revised bill.
sentences.zh: 她收到了一张修改后的账单。

sentences.en: This one was for $1,000.
sentences.zh: 这张是1000美元。

sentences.en: She really has not been able to figure out what the problem here is.
sentences.zh: 她实在弄不清楚问题到底出在哪里。

sentences.en: And of course, the industry is ridiculous.
sentences.zh: 当然，整个行业太荒谬了。

sentences.en: It's suffocating.
sentences.zh: 令人窒息。

sentences.en: And that's a really frequent story.
sentences.zh: 这是一个非常普遍的故事。

sentences.en: I've talked to dozens of people trying to sort this out.
sentences.zh: 我和几十个试图理清这件事的人谈过。

sentences.en: It's an albatross around my neck.
sentences.zh: 这就像挂在我脖子上的沉重负担。

sentences.en: I want it off.
sentences.zh: 我想甩掉它。

sentences.en: I literally lose sleep over this.
sentences.zh: 我真的为这事失眠。

sentences.en: I have nightmares about this.
sentences.zh: 我经常做这方面的噩梦。

sentences.en: My payments are so insanely high.
sentences.zh: 我的还款额高得离谱。

sentences.en: People got really used to not having that payment.
sentences.zh: 人们已经习惯了不用还这笔钱。

sentences.en: And now, with this payment kind of crashing back into their lives, people are trying to make it happen.
sentences.zh: 而现在，随着这笔还款再次闯入他们的生活，人们正努力让它成真。

sentences.en: They know it's a debt they borrowed and one that they have to repay.
sentences.zh: 他们知道这是一笔自己借的债，而且是一笔必须偿还的债。

sentences.en: And they're running into challenges.
sentences.zh: 但他们遇到了挑战。

sentences.en: So I called the Department of Education and waited on hold for hours.
sentences.zh: 所以我打电话给教育部，苦苦等待了好几个小时。

sentences.en: Nobody has any answers.
sentences.zh: 没有人能给出答案。

sentences.en: Nobody has any solutions.
sentences.zh: 没有人有任何解决方案。

sentences.en: Trying to figure out how they can reintegrate this payment into their lives.
sentences.zh: 试图弄清楚他们该如何将这笔还款重新融入自己的生活。

sentences.en: And I'm going, wait a second.
sentences.zh: 而我在想，等等。

sentences.en: I can't make those payments.
sentences.zh: 我根本付不起这些钱。

sentences.en: That's a lot of money.
sentences.zh: 那是一大笔钱。

sentences.en: And then I'll never be able to retire.
sentences.zh: 这样下去我永远也别想退休了。

sentences.en: That's why a big scary shadow chases me in my dreams, literally.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么在我的梦里，真有一个巨大而可怕的阴影在追赶我。

sentences.en: How should we think about the bind that a lot of these folks are in?
sentences.zh: 我们该如何看待这群人所处的困境呢？

sentences.en: I mean, perhaps this is an imperfect analogy.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，也许这个比喻不太完美。

sentences.en: You'll let me know.
sentences.zh: 你会指出来的。

sentences.en: But this feels a bit like the moment when a lot of folks in the mid-2000s who had those adjustable rate mortgages, like, had them reset.
sentences.zh: 但这有点像2000年代中期，很多持有那些可调整利率抵押贷款的人，面临贷款重置的那个时刻。

sentences.en: And all of a sudden, they owed a lot more.
sentences.zh: 突然之间，他们欠了更多的钱。

sentences.en: On some level, they knew that moment would come.
sentences.zh: 从某种程度上说，他们知道那一刻会到来。

sentences.en: And yet when it comes, there's still a lot of financial sting.
sentences.zh: 然而当它真的来临时，依然带来了巨大的财务剧痛。

sentences.en: Even as I'm asking the question, I'm recognizing why it's imperfect.
sentences.zh: 就在我问出这个问题的时候，我也意识到了为什么这个比喻不够完美。

sentences.en: Because in the case of student loans, the situation kept changing.
sentences.zh: 因为在学生贷款的情况下，情况一直在变。

sentences.en: The rules kept changing.
sentences.zh: 规则一直在变。

sentences.en: The expectations kept changing.
sentences.zh: 期望一直在变。

sentences.en: So maybe there's a flaw to that question.
sentences.zh: 所以这个问题可能本身有瑕疵。

sentences.en: How should we think about this?
sentences.zh: 我们该如何看待这件事？

sentences.en: They're very strange loans.
sentences.zh: 这些是非常奇怪的贷款。

sentences.en: There is no other consumer loan that you take out where you don't know when you take it exactly what the payment terms and options are going to be.
sentences.zh: 没有任何其他的消费贷款，你在借款时会不知道确切的还款条件和选项会是什么。

sentences.en: That is really weird.
sentences.zh: 这真的很诡异。

sentences.en: And that has really whiplash people.
sentences.zh: 这真的把人们折腾得够呛。

sentences.en: I mean, most of the borrowers I talk to start the conversation and end the conversation by saying, I want to pay what I owe.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我和大多数借款人交谈时，对话的开始和结束都是在说：我想还清我欠的钱。

sentences.en: I took the loan.
sentences.zh: 我贷了款。

sentences.en: I knew it was going to come due.
sentences.zh: 我知道它会到期。

sentences.en: I knew I'm going to have to pay it.
sentences.zh: 我知道我必须还钱。

sentences.en: But they are really frustrated by both having this hope put in front of them for a more affordable option and then having it snatched away.
sentences.zh: 但他们真的很沮丧，一方面眼前燃起了能享受更实惠选项的希望，另一方面又被无情夺走。

sentences.en: And they're also just really frustrated by the logistics right now of trying to figure out what am I supposed to be doing here?
sentences.zh: 而且他们也对目前的后勤流程感到十分沮丧，不知道自己到底该怎么做。

sentences.en: What has become very evident from this conversation and all the previous conversations we've had with you is that student loans, as managed by the federal government,
sentences.zh: 从这次谈话以及我们之前与你进行的所有谈话中，变得非常明显的一点是，由联邦政府管理的学生贷款，

sentences.en: have become this really variable, wildly unpredictable thing that changes from one president to the next.
sentences.zh: 已经变成了一个多变且完全无法预测的事物，每换一个总统就会发生变化。

sentences.en: And that starts to make me wonder, and I'm guessing I'm not the only one, whether the federal government, with all the political whims of our system,
sentences.zh: 这开始让我怀疑，我猜我也不是唯一一个这样想的人：在经历了我们体制中所有的政治反复无常之后，联邦政府——

sentences.en: is the right institution to be overseeing $1 trillion in student loans.
sentences.zh: 真的是监督一万亿美元学生贷款的合适机构吗？

sentences.en: That's a question that gets asked frequently.
sentences.zh: 这是一个经常被问到的问题。

sentences.en: And certainly the situation right now is bringing it to light again.
sentences.zh: 当然，目前的局势再次让这个问题浮出水面。

sentences.en: And there are people in and around Trump, people in Trump's orbit, who are asking that question and who are raising the issue of,
sentences.zh: 特朗普身边的许多人，也就是特朗普的核心圈子，都在提出这个问题，并引发了讨论：

sentences.en: is it time for the government's role in this to change?
sentences.zh: 现在是时候改变政府在此扮演的角色了吗？

sentences.en: Should the government really play a profoundly different kind of role in this system than it does now?
sentences.zh: 政府在这个体系中扮演的角色，真的应该与现在有深刻的不同吗？

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: I'm Winnalou.
sentences.zh: 我是温纳洛（Winnalou）。

sentences.en: I write the game Connections, one of the puzzles from New York Times games.
sentences.zh: 我是《连线》（Connections）游戏的作者，这是《纽约时报》游戏板块的谜题之一。

sentences.en: And I love horror movies.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢恐怖电影。

sentences.en: I love my dog.
sentences.zh: 我爱我的狗。

sentences.en: And I love trying to trick you.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢试图捉弄你们。

sentences.en: I'm Sam Mazursky, and I create the game Spelling Bee and Letterboxd on a daily basis.
sentences.zh: 我是萨姆·马祖斯基（Sam Mazursky），我每天都设计《拼写蜜蜂》（Spelling Bee）和《Letterboxd》游戏。

sentences.en: And I have this thing called promesthesia.
sentences.zh: 我有一种叫做联觉（promesthesia）的病症。

sentences.en: I see color when I'm listening to music.
sentences.zh: 我在听音乐时能看到颜色。

sentences.en: New York Times games are made by people, like the ones you just heard from.
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》的游戏是由像你刚刚听到的人这样的创作者制作的。

sentences.en: Go to nytimes.com slash games to start playing today.
sentences.zh: 访问 nytimes.com 里的 games 开始今天的游戏吧。

sentences.en: So, Stacey, if, as you just said, there's some real questions about whether the government should play this role in student loans,
sentences.zh: 那么，斯泰西（Stacey），正如你刚才所说，对于政府是否应该在学生贷款中扮演这个角色，存在一些真正的问题，

sentences.en: I think it naturally makes sense to understand how and why the federal government got into this business in the first place.
sentences.zh: 我认为很自然地，我们需要了解联邦政府最初是如何以及为什么涉足这个行业的。

sentences.en: What's that story?
sentences.zh: 背后的故事是什么？

sentences.en: So, for that, we go back to the mid-60s.
sentences.zh: 为此，我们要回到60年代中期。

sentences.en: Up until then, college education and certainly financing for it was something that was pretty limited.
sentences.zh: 在此之前，大学教育以及其资金筹措无疑是相当有限的。

sentences.en: I mean, you really could only get that if you were, you know, a high-performing student studying, you know, hard sciences and things like that.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，只有当你是一名成绩优异、主修硬科学等学科的学生时，你才能真正获得这些资金。

sentences.en: But in 1965, Congress and the president passed the Higher Education Act, and that was a landmark bill that transformed the higher education system.
sentences.zh: 但在1965年，国会和总统通过了《高等教育法》，这是一项具有里程碑意义的法案，改变了高等教育体系。

sentences.en: And it was the first time that said we're going to have a government-sponsored program where pretty much anyone can come get a loan and borrow to go to college.
sentences.zh: 这是第一次提出我们要建立一个由政府资助的项目，几乎任何人都可以来申请贷款并借钱去上大学。

sentences.en: So private banks actually made the loans.
sentences.zh: 所以实际上是由私人银行来发放贷款。

sentences.en: But these are really risky loans.
sentences.zh: 但这些是风险极高的贷款。

sentences.en: A lot of them aren't going to get paid back.
sentences.zh: 其中许多贷款无法偿还。

sentences.en: So the role the government played was it said to the private lenders, okay, if this loan goes bad, if it sours and the borrower doesn't pay, we will step in and pay you.
sentences.zh: 因此，政府扮演的角色是向私人贷款机构表示：好吧，如果这笔贷款坏账了、泡汤了，借款人没有还钱，我们会介入并向你们支付。

sentences.en: Because there's a public interest in sending more and more Americans to college.
sentences.zh: 因为送越来越多的美国人去上大学符合公众利益。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: This was very much perceived as something that was good for the United States.
sentences.zh: 这在很大程度上被视为对美国有益的事情。

sentences.en: Part of it came out of a direct counter to the Soviet Union, the concern that we would fall behind, that there would be an education gap.
sentences.zh: 部分原因是对苏联的直接回应，人们担心我们会落后，会出现教育鸿沟。

sentences.en: So the idea was that this was something that was in the taxpayers' interests to make sure that more people could pursue higher education.
sentences.zh: 因此，当时的理念是，确保更多人能够接受高等教育符合纳税人的利益。

sentences.en: So how did that go, the government being the backstop?
sentences.zh: 那么，作为最后防线的政府，进展得怎么样？

sentences.en: Rocky.
sentences.zh: 一波三折。

sentences.en: The program went through a lot of changes over the years.
sentences.zh: 这些年来，该计划经历了很多变化。

sentences.en: The banks were making money doing this, and the government was taking on the administrative burden of running the programs and of backstopping them.
sentences.zh: 银行通过这样做在赚钱，而政府则承担着运营这些项目以及提供兜底的行政负担。

sentences.en: So they would take on the losses when the loans soured.
sentences.zh: 所以当贷款变坏账时，他们要承担损失。

sentences.en: And there was certainly criticism that came up from time to time about, hey, why are we letting the banks make all the profit here while we're subsidizing all of the risk?
sentences.zh: 当然，时不时也会出现这样的批评：嘿，为什么我们在补贴所有风险的同时，却让银行赚取所有的利润？

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对的。

sentences.en: A reasonable question.
sentences.zh: 这是一个合理的问题。

sentences.en: Mm-hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯嗯。

sentences.en: So fast-forwarding a little bit, how do we arrive at a moment where the federal government decides maybe we will take on both the risk and the reward?
sentences.zh: 那么快进一点，我们是如何走到这一步的：联邦政府决定也许我们应该同时承担风险和回报？

sentences.en: So the moment when everything changed was in 2010 as part of the Affordable Care Act, weirdly enough.
sentences.zh: 一切改变的时刻是在2010年，当时它作为《平价医疗法案》的一部分出台，说来也奇怪。

sentences.en: So President Obama wanted to pass the Affordable Care Act, this very massive and expensive change in the health care system.
sentences.zh: 当时奥巴马总统想要通过《平价医疗法案》，这是医疗体系中规模庞大且费用高昂的一项变革。

sentences.en: And the government went looking for what it calls pay-fors.
sentences.zh: 于是政府开始寻找他们所谓的“资金来源”（pay-fors）。

sentences.en: It went looking for ways to—
sentences.zh: 它开始寻找途径来——

sentences.en: Revenue generators.
sentences.zh: 创收渠道。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Things that they could put into the budget and say, look, we're now making money, so this is going to balance out.
sentences.zh: 他们可以塞进预算里并说，看，我们现在赚钱了，所以这会收支相抵。

sentences.en: And this was the area they zeroed in on.
sentences.zh: 这就是他们锁定的领域。

sentences.en: Student loans.
sentences.zh: 学生贷款。

sentences.en: Mm-hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯嗯。

sentences.en: Even though they don't make any money from it.
sentences.zh: 尽管他们从中赚不到任何钱。

sentences.en: Well, that was the calculation.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这就是当时的算盘。

sentences.en: The Congressional Budget Office and other financial analysts came back and said, if you take this in-house,
sentences.zh: 国会预算办公室和其他金融分析师给出反馈称，如果你把这收归国有——

sentences.en: if you start making these loans directly and keeping the profits from them, that's going to generate tens of billions of dollars over the next decade for the government.
sentences.zh: 如果你开始直接发放这些贷款并保留其中的利润，这将在未来十年内为政府带来数百亿美元的收入。

sentences.en: And for the first few years, that is how it starts to play out.
sentences.zh: 在最初的几年里，事情确实是按这个方向发展的。

sentences.en: And then that starts to change.
sentences.zh: 然后情况开始发生变化。

sentences.en: For kind of two reasons.
sentences.zh: 原因主要有两个。

sentences.en: The first is that the amount of money people owe starts to really surge.
sentences.zh: 首先是人们欠款的金额开始真正飙升。

sentences.en: And that both makes it significantly harder for them to pay it off.
sentences.zh: 而且这也让他们偿还债务的难度大大增加。

sentences.en: You start to see more defaults and more people struggling with this debt.
sentences.zh: 你会开始看到更多违约情况，以及更多人为这笔债务苦苦挣扎。

sentences.en: And it also starts incentivizing the government to look at ways to make it more affordable.
sentences.zh: 这也开始激励政府寻找让其更能负担得起的方法。

sentences.en: So you start to see them introduce more loan forgiveness programs, more repayment options that are more generous and more flexible,
sentences.zh: 所以你开始看到他们推出更多贷款减免计划、更慷慨、更灵活的还款选项，

sentences.en: things where it means that the government starts to be subsidizing this program.
sentences.zh: 这意味着政府开始补贴这个计划。

sentences.en: And making less money.
sentences.zh: 而且赚的钱更少了。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: The math on this starts to change.
sentences.zh: 这里的账目开始发生变化。

sentences.en: And this moves from being an income center to the government to an area of projected losses.
sentences.zh: 这从政府的收入中心变成了预计亏损的领域。

sentences.en: Was there a conversation in this period about whether the government's approach to this is making college more expensive?
sentences.zh: 在这期间，有没有人讨论过政府的方法是否让上大学变得更贵了？

sentences.en: Oh, yes.
sentences.zh: 哦，有的。

sentences.en: Because that seems like a clear link.
sentences.zh: 因为这看起来是一个明显的联系。

sentences.en: If the government is the provider of these loans and it's going to forgive lots of the loans as they get bigger and bigger,
sentences.zh: 如果政府是这些贷款的提供者，并且随着贷款越来越多，它打算减免大量贷款，

sentences.en: what incentive do colleges and universities have to put a cap on the price of going to college?
sentences.zh: 那学院和大学有什么动力去限制上大学的费用上限呢？

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 完全同意。

sentences.en: That's been a running conversation for at least 20 plus years.
sentences.zh: 这是一个至少持续了20多年的老话题了。

sentences.en: Even before the government pulled this all in-house, there was concerns from economists and policy analysts that this was driving the cost of tuition going up.
sentences.zh: 甚至在政府把这一切收归国有之前，经济学家和政策分析人士就担心这正在推高学费成本。

sentences.en: Again, there's no other loans that really work like this.
sentences.zh: 再说一次，没有其他贷款是真正这样运作的。

sentences.en: If you're borrowing for your undergraduate degree, you can borrow tens of thousands of dollars.
sentences.zh: 如果你是为了读本科而借贷，你可以借到几万美元。

sentences.en: And if you're borrowing for a graduate degree, you can borrow basically an unlimited amount of money.
sentences.zh: 如果你是为了读研究生而借贷，你基本上可以借到无限金额的钱。

sentences.en: There's no test of are you likely to be able to make enough to pay this.
sentences.zh: 这里没有测试你是否有能力赚到足够的钱来偿还。

sentences.en: So that's how you get to a place where when you basically hand students and really hand the schools a blank check, suddenly the price goes up a lot.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么当你基本上递给学生、实际上是递给学校一张空白支票时，价格突然大幅上涨。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Well, for the sake of argument, what would it look like for the federal government to get out of the student loan business
sentences.zh: 好吧，为了辩论起见，如果联邦政府退出学生贷款业务，

sentences.en: and to return to the pre-Obama era where it's really the private sector in charge of this?
sentences.zh: 回到奥巴马时代之前、真正由私营部门负责的时期，会是什么样子？

sentences.en: And would that likely create a more predictable, less confusing, whip-sawing system?
sentences.zh: 这会不会更有可能创建一个更可预测、更少混乱、不会剧烈波动的系统？

sentences.en: And just to make this question even more complicated, might that lower the cost of tuition?
sentences.zh: 为了让这个问题更复杂一点，这会不会降低学费成本？

sentences.en: I think the answer to all of that is it's unclear.
sentences.zh: 我认为所有这些问题的答案都是不确定的。

sentences.en: There's a lot of different options for how you could change the system if you were going to.
sentences.zh: 如果要改变系统，你有很多不同的选择。

sentences.en: You could simply go back to the pre-2010 system and just say, this is the banks and we're just here to backstop it.
sentences.zh: 你可以简单地回到2010年之前的系统，然后说，这是银行的业务，我们只是来提供后盾的。

sentences.en: So that's one possibility.
sentences.zh: 所以这是一种可能性。

sentences.en: As for tuition, I think people think the biggest issue there would be capping the amount that people can borrow.
sentences.zh: 至于学费，我认为人们认为最大的问题将是设定借款金额上限。

sentences.en: Banks potentially might say, this is the limit you can take, which currently doesn't exiSt.
sentences.zh: 银行可能会说，这是你可以借的限额，而目前这并不存在。

sentences.en: Banks or the government or someone coming in and putting a limit in place because that would force the schools to respond to that.
sentences.zh: 银行或政府或其他某方介入并设定限额，因为这会迫使学校做出回应。

sentences.en: Right now, a lot of what's driven tuition is that they can do it.
sentences.zh: 目前，推高学费的很大一部分原因在于他们可以这么做。

sentences.en: And nobody is sort of forcing a price constraint here.
sentences.zh: 而且这里没有人强加价格限制。

sentences.en: Mm-hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯哼。

sentences.en: Is it fair to ask whether what Trump is doing here, by forcing the system to go back to its original state five years ago,
sentences.zh: 一个公平的问题是，特朗普在这里所做的事——通过迫使系统回到五年前的最初状态，

sentences.en: is that he is forcing us to reckon with all the things we're talking about here and to perhaps rethink the government's role.
sentences.zh: 是不是在迫使我们正视我们在这里谈论的所有事情，并或许重新思考政府的角色。

sentences.en: And is that a healthy exercise because of the confusion, because of the tuition costs that are unconstrained by the current system?
sentences.zh: 考虑到混乱，考虑到当前系统没有受到约束的学费成本，这是否是一次健康的锻炼？

sentences.en: I mean, how many times in this conversation have you basically said the system is broken?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，在这段对话中，你有多少次基本上说过这个系统已经崩溃了？

sentences.en: Biden was trying to fix it through ad hoc amnesty and forbearance.
sentences.zh: 拜登试图通过临时的特赦和宽限来解决这个问题。

sentences.en: Is what Trump is trying to do here a very different version of fixing it through a kind of brute force, tough medicine?
sentences.zh: 特朗普在这里试图做的，是不是通过一种蛮力、下猛药的方式来解决它的一个截然不同的版本？

sentences.en: Certainly the fact that we are on track right now for huge numbers of delinquencies, huge numbers of defaults,
sentences.zh: 当然，我们目前正面临着大量拖欠、大量违约的趋势，

sentences.en: that creates the conditions in which you would hope people would take a close look at the system and say, what can be done better?
sentences.zh: 这创造了一种环境，让你希望人们能仔细审视这个系统并说：有什么可以做得更好的？

sentences.en: How can we fix this?
sentences.zh: 我们该如何解决这个问题？

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: That said, part of why we've had this conversation so many times is that's kind of been the shape of the system for much of the last decade
sentences.zh: 话虽如此，我们之所以这么多次进行这样的对话，部分原因是因为在过去十年里的大部分时间里，

sentences.en: across multiple presidential administrations, Democratic and Republican.
sentences.zh: 在多届民主党和共和党总统任期内，系统的形态一直都是这样。

sentences.en: This has been for a very long time a really broken system.
sentences.zh: 长期以来，这是一个真正崩溃的系统。

sentences.en: And unless Trump does try to take it out of the government's hands or do something pretty radical, he will simply extend the brokenness.
sentences.zh: 除非特朗普真的试图把它从政府手中夺走，或者做一些相当激进的事情，否则他只会延续这种崩溃。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Without any upside.
sentences.zh: 没有任何好处。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And that's what we just don't know.
sentences.zh: 而这正是我们所不知道的。

sentences.en: I mean, really, there's a lot of options here, but the administration has not laid out any clear policy plans whatsoever here.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，实际上，这里有很多选择，但政府根本没有提出任何明确的政策计划。

sentences.en: So no one's clear on is this a moment when we're actually going to make critical changes to the system
sentences.zh: 所以没有人弄清楚，这究竟是一个我们将对系统进行重大变革的时刻，

sentences.en: or are we just going to do what we've been doing for a long time now of limping along with this broken system
sentences.zh: 还是我们只是在重复长期以来一直在做的事情——带着这个崩溃的系统苦苦支撑，

sentences.en: and leaving borrowers to kind of fend for themselves in dealing with it.
sentences.zh: 让借款人自己去应付。

sentences.en: And if that is the case, if the system limps and borrowers are left to pay these huge bills,
sentences.zh: 如果真是这样，如果系统在苦苦支撑，而借款人不得不支付这些巨额账单，

sentences.en: I want to go back to something you said in the beginning about delinquency and default.
sentences.zh: 我想回到你一开始说的关于拖欠和违约的话题。

sentences.en: What does the world look like in six to nine months, a year, a year and a half, if we start to see those millions of defaults?
sentences.zh: 如果我们开始看到数以百万计的违约，六到九个月、一年、一年半后的世界会是什么样子？

sentences.en: It's obviously really catastrophic for individual people and their households.
sentences.zh: 这显然对个人及其家庭来说是真正的灾难。

sentences.en: The effects of delinquencies and defaults really stick with you.
sentences.zh: 拖欠和违约的影响确实会长期伴随着你。

sentences.en: For delinquencies, it's going to mess up your credit score.
sentences.zh: 对于拖欠而言，它会搞砸你的信用评分。

sentences.en: It's going to make it really hard for you to get loans and financing.
sentences.zh: 它会让你很难获得贷款和融资。

sentences.en: It's going to make it much more expensive for you to do that.
sentences.zh: 它会让你这样做的成本高昂得多。

sentences.en: That often stops people from being able to afford the things they need for their daily lives, from housing to a car to things like that.
sentences.zh: 这往往让人无力承担日常生活所需的东西，从住房到汽车，再到诸如此类的事情。

sentences.en: But it's also bad for the economy writ large.
sentences.zh: 但这对手头整体经济也是不利的。

sentences.en: If people are having to really constrain their household spending, you're not going out to dinner, you're not going out with your friends, things like that.
sentences.zh: 如果人们不得不大幅收紧家庭开支，你就不去吃晚餐了，不和朋友出去了，诸如此类。

sentences.en: Right, it's just a wet blanket over the entire economy.
sentences.zh: 没错，这就像给整个经济泼了一盆冷水。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 正是如此。

sentences.en: So that's one area of concern.
sentences.zh: 所以这是一个令人担忧的领域。

sentences.en: It also sort of does raise the broader question about the entire system, about is this worth it?
sentences.zh: 它也确实提出了关于整个系统的更广泛问题：这一切真的值得吗？

sentences.en: You do see people, teenagers, people in their early 20s, questioning the concept, saying, do I want to go to college?
sentences.zh: 你确实看到人们，青少年，20岁出头的人，在质疑这个概念，在说：我想上大学吗？

sentences.en: Do I want to take on tens of thousands or hundreds of thousands of debt that's going to chase me around for decades and decades?
sentences.zh: 我想背负几万或几十万将纠缠我几十年的债务吗？

sentences.en: And that does sort of take us back to right where we were in the 60s, of deciding how much we as a society want to invest in this
sentences.zh: 这确实让我们回到了60年代的起点，去决定我们作为一个社会愿意在这个上面投资多少，

sentences.en: and how broadly available higher education really will be.
sentences.zh: 以及高等教育到底能普及到什么程度。

sentences.en: Well, Stacey, appreciate your time.
sentences.zh: 好吧，斯黛西，感谢你的时间。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你。

sentences.en: As always, thanks.
sentences.zh: 一如既往，谢谢。

sentences.en: Thanks.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: Here's what else you need to know today.
sentences.zh: 以下是你今天需要了解的其他消息。

sentences.en: On Sunday night, The Times reported that Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth shared detailed information about forthcoming airstrikes in Yemen in yet another signal messaging chat,
sentences.zh: 周日晚上，《泰晤士报》报道称，国防部长皮特·海格塞斯在另一个信号聊天群里分享了关于也门即将进行的空袭的详细信息，

sentences.en: this time with a group that included his wife, brother, and personal lawyer.
sentences.zh: 这一次的群成员包括他的妻子、兄弟和私人律师。

sentences.en: The latest revelation raises even more questions about Hegseth's judgment and about Trump's decision to appoint Hegseth to oversee the U.S.
sentences.zh: 最新曝光的信息引发了更多关于海格塞斯判断力的质疑，也让人对特朗普任命海格塞斯负责美国

sentences.en: military.
sentences.zh: 军方的决定产生疑问。

sentences.en: Today's episode was produced by Rob Zipko, Stella Tan, and Rochelle Bonjana.
sentences.zh: 今天的节目由罗布·齐普科、斯特拉·谭和罗谢尔·邦贾纳制作。

sentences.en: It was edited by Devin Taylor and Patricia Willans.
sentences.zh: 由德文·泰勒和帕特里夏·威兰斯剪辑。

sentences.en: Contains original music by Rowan Emisto, Marion Lozano, and Dan Powell.
sentences.zh: 包含罗恩·埃米斯托、马里昂·洛扎诺和丹·鲍威尔的原创音乐。

sentences.en: And was engineered by Chris Wood.
sentences.zh: 由克里斯·伍德担任音频工程。

sentences.en: Our theme music is by Jim Brunberg and Ben Landsberg of Wonderland.
sentences.zh: 我们的主题曲由来自仙境的吉姆·布伦伯格和本·兰兹伯格创作。

sentences.en: That's it for The Daily.
sentences.zh: 这就是今天的《每日新闻》。

sentences.en: I'm Michael Bavaro.
sentences.zh: 我是迈克尔·巴瓦罗。

sentences.en: See you tomorrow.
sentences.zh: 明天见。

sentences.en: For decades, the Brooklyn Democratic Party operated as a tightly controlled machine.
sentences.zh: 几十年来，布鲁克林民主党一直作为一个受严密控制的机器运作。

sentences.en: Until this summer.
sentences.zh: 直到今年夏天。

sentences.en: When elections ushered in a bunch of self-described reformers.
sentences.zh: 当时选举迎来了群自称改革派的人。

sentences.en: Ever since, the party has been in the grip of a bruising, chaotic, and sometimes thrilling fight.
sentences.zh: 从那以后，该党一直陷入一场残酷、混乱、有时又扣人心弦的斗争中。

sentences.en: In the latest episode of Metro with me, Sarah Koenig, stories of people trying to maintain their influence and losing control along the way.
sentences.zh: 在我和萨拉·科尼格主持的最新一期《都市》节目中，讲述了人们试图保持影响力却在过程中失去控制的故事。

sentences.en: Metro.
sentences.zh: 《都市》。

sentences.zh: 请在您获取播客的任何地方收听。
